data.hypothesis: Keeping one target per thread and a 128-thread CTA while doubling the source tile from 256 to 512 should halve the tile-loop and barrier-pair count for each target block. The tradeoff is twice the shared-memory footprint (8 KiB) and four cooperative loads per thread per tile, so official timing must determine whether the reduced synchronization overhead helps.
data.notes: The launch uses a 512-record tile of four floats per record and 128 targets per CTA. All threads reach both barriers, source and target tails are guarded, self-interactions are excluded by global index, and each active target writes once. No commands or measurements were run; controller correctness and timing remain authoritative.
transformations: Changed the launch to 128 threads/targets per CTA with 8192 bytes of dynamic shared memory for 512 compact source records.
Cooperatively staged bounded source chunks and synchronized before use and before replacing each chunk, with inactive tail threads participating in barriers.
Kept one target and force accumulator per active thread, skipped self-interactions by global index, preserved the force and integration expressions, and guarded partial tiles and target tails.
